She took the head and went to the place where Sambal Singh was seated. ‘, the way you told me, I have done. ‘Here, I put the Quazi’s head in front of you. ‘Even if you want my head, I can give it to you, ‘Because I love you from, both, my heart and soul. ‘Oh! my lover, Whatever the word you gave me, you fulfil this very evening. ‘Through the winks of your eyes, you have captured my soul.‘ When the Raja looked at the severed-head, he became fearful, And said, ‘Oh! You the devilish, ‘If you have treated your husband so wickedly, ‘Then what would you not do to me? ‘I am better off without your friendship, I renounce your fraternity. ‘Your deed has dreaded me.’ ‘You have treated your husband in such a bad manner, ‘You may administer your ill-designs on me too. She threw the head there and then, And started to beat her chest and head with her hands. ‘You have turned your back on me and God will turn his on you, ‘And that will be the day of God’s judgement upon you.’ Throwing the head there, she returned to her house. Lying besides the dead-body of the Quazi, she went to sleep., put dust in her hair, and shouted. ‘Oh! My pious friends, get here, ‘Some evil man has committed an evil act. ‘With one stroke he has killed the Quazi.’ Following the traces of blood, people started to proceed, And they all took the same path. She brought all the people to that place, Where she had thrown the Quazi’s head. The woman convinced the people, That the Raja had killed the Quazi. They got hold of the Raja and tied him, And brought him there, where the Jehangir was seated on his throne. The Emperor thought, ‘If I hand over to the Quazi’s wife, ‘She will deal with him the way she wanted.’ Then he ordered the executioner, ‘Slay the head of this man with one hard stroke.’ When that young man saw the sword, He started to shake like a huge cypress tree. And whispered, ‘Whatever bad deed I performed, ‘I did it to capture your heart.’ Then, winking, he added, ‘Oh you the Lady among all the ladies. ‘And the Queen among all the Queens, ‘If I disobeyed you, I committed a sin. ‘I committed this act without thinking and without asking you, ‘Now, let me go free. I will obey your command, ‘And I say this to swear upon the God. ‘I have perpetrated, please forgive me, ‘I will remain your slave.’ She soliloquised, ‘If I kill five hundred Rajas like him, ‘Even then Quazi will not come to life.’ ‘Now when Quazi is dead, why should I kill him too? ‘Why should I take the curse of killing him upon myself? ‘Wouldn’t it be better if I let him go free, ‘And proceed on pilgrimage to Kabah at Mecca.’ Saying so, she let loose him, Then she went home and collected a few prominent people. She gathered her goods, got ready and preyed, ‘Please God, help me to fulfil my ambition. ‘I regret that I am going away from my fraternity, ‘If I remain alive, I may come back.’ She put all her money, jewellery and other precious articles in the bundles, ‘And commenced her journey towards the House of Allah at Kabah.‘ When she had covered three stages of her voyage, She thought of the house of her friend. At midnight, she returned to his house, Along with all sort of gifts and souvenirs. The people of the world never realised, where had she gone. And no body cared what state of affairs she had been passing through?, ‘Oh! Saki, Give me the cup full of green, ‘Which I need at the time of my nourishment. ‘Give it to me so that I can contemplate, ‘As it kindles my thought like an earthen-lamp.’
17.5: The Lord is One and the Victory is of the True Guru. God, Almighty is benevolent in forgiveness, He is Enlightener, Provider and Guide. Neither He has an army nor luxurious living. God, the Compassionate, is visible and manifested. Now, please listen to the tale of the daughter of a minister. She was very pretty and possessed an enlightened mind. There lived a wandering Prince who had adorned himself with Cap from Rome. His splendour matched the sun but his nature was as serene as the Moon. Once, early in the morning he went out hunting. He took with him a hound, a falcon and a hawk. He reached a desolate place of hunting. The Prince killed the lions, leopards and deer. There came another Raja from the South, Who roared like a lion and his face gleamed like the moon. Both the rulers had approached an intricate terrain. Are not the lucky ones only rescued through their swords? Doesn’t an auspicious day facilitate one? Who is endowed aid by the God of gods? Both the rulers flew in the rage, Like the two lions that sprawl over a hunted deer. Thundering like the black clouds both jumped forward. Like the leaves flutter during the dust storm, the arrows started to fly. The arrows flew in such density that, The sky was inundated with vultures. Noises coming through the tips of the spears were piercing, And both were creating havoc in the world. They were raising hue and cries, as if, to seek final bliss of Angel of Resurrection, So that, on the doomsday, they attain sanctuary in the heaven. At the end anarchy surrounded the Arabian Army, And western Raja had the victorious day. The Arabian Prince was isolated, When the sun set in the evening. As he had lost all his power, he tried to escape, But could not, he surrendered and become a prisoner. The Prince was tied down and taken to the Raja, The same way as Rahu, the demon planet, captured the moon. Although the news of the Prince’s arrest reached his household, In spite of hard efforts Prince could not be rescued. The wise ones assembled in the Court, And talked over the shame. When the daughter of the Minister heard the news, She girded up her lions and tucked the arrows in there. Adoring the dress of the country of Rome, She mounted the horse. Galloping in the winds, she approached the Raja of the West, With Kiani Clan’s quiver full of arrows at her back. She faced the Raja with great courage, But she, who used to roar like the thundering clouds and carnivorous lions, Bowed in greeting and said, ‘Oh! You the fortunate Raja, ‘Worthy of Royal Throne and the Royal Canopy. ‘My grass-cutters had come to shear the grass, ‘They were riding hundreds of horses and one of them looked like the Prince. ‘You better send them back, “Otherwise, there will be a call for your death. “If my King heard this from me, “He would come to uproot you.” The Raja of iron will heard this, And started to tremble like the leaves of jasmine shrubs. The Raja thought, ‘If these grass-cutters had given such a tough fight, ‘Then their King must a very brave man. ‘I did not perceive that their King was so brave, ‘That he would drag me, even, out of hell.’ The Raja called his Counsellors, And had a secret conversation with them, ‘Oh! My Counsellors, you have seen the grass-cutters fighting so vigorously, ‘And the havoc they had brought to this God’s country. ‘God forbid, if that King raided, then this country would be ruined. ‘I should return the grass-cutters to this lucky one.’ The Raja immediately called the tied-up grass-cutter, Invited him besides him and, then, handed him over., ‘You have easily attained the freedom, ‘Now you apprehend them. I love you more than my life’. She held the folds of her turban with one hand, And put the other hand on the scabbard of her sword, She gave four lashes to each one of them, And said, ‘You, the ignorant, you don’t know anything. ‘You have come here where there is no grass to cut. ‘The God only is my witness,’ ‘God is my Protector, ‘He is Forgiver and, I am sure, He will excuse my lie.‘ After gaining freedom for his sovereign, She left that place for her own abode., ‘Oh! Saki, give me green wine to drink, Because the Master of the Intellect prevails all over. ‘Saki! Give me the cup full of greenish, “Which soothes during the wars and the lonely nights.”
17.6: The Lord is One and the Victory is of the True Guru. God is all-benevolent, He is luminously manifest and dominates all the domains. His will prevails, and his blessedness is splendid, And the splendid blessedness is epitome of sagacity. When Asphand Yaar departed from this world taking all his belongings with him, He conferred the sovereignty to his son, Bahmin. That Bahmin had a daughter, who was like the wings of phoenix. And she was elegantly graceful and quite affluent When Bahmin, as well, departed from this world facing his destiny, He bestowed the sovereignty to his daughter. She was the one, who was like the phoenix of Rome, Spread over to progress like the spring season. When fourteen years had gone by and she became teen-ager, Her charm gained the full swing. She reached the same stage, As the rose flower which bloomed in the garden. Her beauty enchanted like the blue bird that scintillated in the spring, And like the moon that adorned itself in joyous weather. The childlike innocence was still depicting, When the flavour of youth descended on her. When all her childhood flew away, And the spell of adolescence over powered, Then she enthroned herself on the royal seat, And pondered over the regal papers prevalent there. Once she came across an appraiser of diamonds, And, taking the advantage of darkness, she took him inside. She kept him in for two, three, four months, And through the semen of that tycoon, she became pregnant. When nine month have gone by, The delightful lady felt movement of child birth. She gave birth to a milk-sucking Prince, Who would become the ruler and exterminator of the opposing rulers. She had not disclosed the secret of his birth, And had placed him in a box, away from the sight of others. She applied musk and perfumed it in Otto. Then she coated it with saffron, and kindled incense around. After placing a red stone in his hands, She pushed the box into the deep flowing water. Immediately after the launching, she tore off her clothes, And sat down to prey God to protect him. The washermen sitting on the bank of the river, Noticed the box drifting in the river. They decided to fetch the box out, And break it open. Using the power of their arms they pulled the box out, And on its fringes they found lot of precious things. When they opened it using further force, They came across more precious articles. They broke its seal, And inside, they found him dazzling like the moon. The washer men had no children, They thought, ‘God has endowed us with a son.’ As they had rescued him from the deep water, They thanked God for endowing them such a cherished gift. They brought him up like their son, And went to Mecca on pilgrimage as well. When two or three years and a few months had gone past, The daughter of the washer man, brought him to the king’s palace. The great phoenix went into deep thought on seeing him, But, then, realised that he was the son of a washer man. He asked, “Oh, you the kind lady, “How did you get a son so handsome in stature, and so sober in habits.” She thought, ‘It is me only who knows the secret. ‘No body else knows what is the truth.’ The person wanted to take away her son, and Quickly proceeded to the house of the washerwoman. The washerwoman said, “I will tell you, how did I find him, ‘I will narrate to you, how did I discover him.‘ ‘In such a year and at such day, in the evening, ‘I performed all this task. ‘I got hold of the box in deep water, ‘When I opened it, I found him there, and that is the truth. ‘On seeing him, I felt the milk dripping out of my breasts, ‘And I took both his hands on them. ‘Recognising the place, his both the lips opened. ‘I never revealed this secret to anybody.’ The same wife went to next day and said, ‘In my dream I had a vision of a pious man, ‘, “I have endowed you the son, ‘“I have done so to edify the glory of Kian Clan.’” The king kept the boy at home and Gave him the treasure, gold, diamond and the throne, And said, ‘As I have secured him through the river, ‘I name him, Darab. ‘I bestow upon him the temporal kingdom, ‘And I crown him with regal honour and imperial fly-whisk. ‘I admire his status, ‘Because his posture is majestic.” learned, as well, that he had become a king, And that he was given the name, Darab. The gallant one promoted the righteous rule, Because he was the seeker of truth, and he believed in virtuosity. ‘Oh! Saki, give me green wine to drink, ‘Because the Master is intelligent enough, and is known all over. ‘Saki! Give me the cup full of greenish, ‘Which soothes during the wars and the lonely nights.’
17.7: The Lord is One and the Victory is of the True Guru. God endows tranquillity, He grants the will to believe, provides living and contentment. He is Sovereign of both the worlds, He keeps us all away from afflictions. Now listen to the Tale of King Azam, Who was magnanimous and compassionate. With perfect posture, his countenance radiated. Whole day he used to spend listening to the musical renderings of Ragas, and quaffing cups of wine. He was renown for his wisdom, And was famous for magnanimity of his bravery. He had a moon-like pretty wife, The people admired the exquisiteness of his preference. She was very beautiful and possessed sober temperament with captivating features. Also she enjoyed sweat voice, dressed herself profusely, and was chaste in her thought. She had two sons, called Sun and Moon. Intellectually content, they always aspired for the truth. Being very fast in their hand movements, they were clever in fights. They were like the roaring lions and vicious like crocodiles. Those lion-hearted could subdue the elephants, And during the wars they became embodiment of steel. Not only they had attractive features, their bodies gleamed like silver. Both the figures called for highest acclaims. Their mother fell in love with a stranger, Because that man was like a flower, and their mother was in search of such a flower. They had just come into their sleeping chamber, When they caught sight of both the undaunted ones. They called in both the younger and older one, And entertained them with wine and music through the Raga Singers. When she realised that they were absolutely intoxicated, She stood up and cut their heads with the sword. Then she started to beat her head with both her hands, And began to tremble and shout very loudly, She shouted, ‘Oh, you the pious Muslims, ‘How they have cut each other like the scissors cut the clothes? ‘Both of them drenched themselves in wine, ‘And took the swords in their hands, ‘One hit the other and, right in front of my eyes, they murdered each other. ‘Hai, why didn’t earth give way to obscure myself in there, ‘Even the door of the hell has been closed for me. ‘Down with my eyes, ‘The eyes which were watching when they killed each other. ‘You abandoned this world, ‘I will, now, become an ascetic and go to the Country of China.’ Pronouncing thus, she tore off her clothes, And proceeded towards the bewilderment. She went to a location where there was restful place. There, on the back of a bullock, she saw Shiva, along with women as pretty as the moon. He asked her, ‘Oh, you the kind woman, ‘Slim and tall like a cypress tree, who are you? ‘Are you either a Soul or a Fairy? ‘Are you either the moon in the sky or sun over the earth?’, ‘Neither I am Fairy, nor an Enlightener of the world. ‘I am the daughter of the King of Zablistan.’ Then, on learning, she supplicated, Opened her mouth, and narrated very gently., ‘I am much afflicted on seeing you. ‘Whatever you desire I will grant you.’, ‘I should get out of the old age and become young again, ‘So that I can go to the country of my lover.‘, ‘If you think this appropriate according to your intelligence, ‘Although it may have come in your mind very menially.’ After receiving the boon, she came to the well, Where her lover used to come for hunting. Next day she came across the hunter, Who had sharp features like the sparrow-hawk in the spring. On seeing him, she started to run forward like a wild cow. And he galloped his horse at the speed of an arrow. They went quite far, Where there was no water and no food, and they were lost in themselves. She proceeded and bodily joined that young-man, As there was none other like him, neither soul nor body. Immediately on her sight, he had fallen in love with her, And lost his senses and consciousness. ‘I swear by God that I must do with you, ‘Because I cherish you more than my own life.’ The woman, just to show off, refused a few times, But, at the end she acquiesced. Look at the infidelity of the world, Siavash were annihilated without any vestiges. Where have gone the Kings, Khusro and Jamshed? Where are Adam and Muhammad? Where have vanished the kings, Faraid, Bahmin and Asfand? Neither Darab, nor Dara are esteemed. What happened to Alexander and Sher Shah? None of them has survived. How Temur Shah and Babar have dissipated? Where did Hamayun and Akbar had gone? ‘Oh! Saki. Give me the reddish wine of Europe. ‘Which I would relish when I brandish the sword during the war. ‘Give it to me so that I could contemplate, ‘And with the sword annihilate.’
17.8: The Lord is One and the Victory is of the True Guru. He is absolute, divine, eminent, and compassionate. The destiny-prevailer, the sustainer, the eliminator of bondage and considerate. To the devotees, He has endowed the earth, the sky. The temporal world and the heavens. Now listen to the tale of a foreign emperor, Who was sitting on the bedstead besides his wife. She looked out and saw the son of a jeweller, Who appeared to be very handsome and at the prime of his youth. When the sun had set she summoned, The handsome boy, who was tall like a cypress tree. They both embraced each other and blended into one, All their senses, uniqueness and attributes. Any body who would see him, could not judge the reality, As his male face had been disguised as female. Every body conceded that he was a lady, And she was as pretty as the heavenly fairies. One day the king saw her, And complimented that her features were enchanting like the moon in the sky. She was, then, counselled, ‘You the lucky one, ‘You are worthy of a king and fit to sit on the throne.’ ‘Whose woman are you and whose daughter are you? ‘Which country you belong to and whose sister are you? ‘You have penetrated the inner vision, ‘And has the king fallen for you at the first sight.’ Through his maid, the king called her, And asked her to bring her to the inner chambers of his house. ‘Oh, my maid, I have come across an elegant like a cypress tree, ‘Which looks like the moon fallen from the skies of Yaman. ‘My heart is writhing for her, ‘It is like fish flutters when it is thrown in a dirty puddle. ‘Oh, you my maid-messenger, who are like a blooming flower, ‘Go to the blossoming bud and bring her to me. ‘If you bring her to me for me, ‘I will open up all the annuls of my treasures for you.’ Harking to this the maidservant instantly departed, And narrated from head to tail of the whole conservation. When she listened to the whole talk from the maid, Feeling topsy-turvy, he was overpowered with distress. ‘If I reveal my secret to the world, ‘All my planning will be dismantled. ‘Looking at my female attire, the king has fallen for me, ‘Oh, my lady, please counsel me what to do?’ ‘If you say so, I will run away from this place. ‘Immediately, today, I take on my heels.’ ‘Don’t be afraid, I will tell you the remedy. ‘Even remaining under his observation, I will keep you for four months.’ Then, they both went to the sleeping-place and went into a slumber, And the news roamed around to the lion hearted king. The maid, then, conveyed the king what was happening, And the king flew into rage from head to feet. Instantly he came to the palace of the queen, And seeing them in the same bed, became inflammable like the sun. The king assumed that she had discerned his intentions, And had become very cautious. That is why they went into sleep at the same place and in the same bed. ‘God forbid, she made my attempt impossible. ‘If I had found her alone in the bedroom, ‘I would have at once clung to her as the moon merged into the sun.’ The king returned that night lamenting, And the second day again he saw them sleeping in the same style. ‘Had I found her sleeping alone, ‘I would have pounced upon her like a lion.’ He went away on the second day and again appeared on the third day. As usual, seeing them together he departed. On the fourth day they were joined together again. He hung his head in astonishment and thought, ‘Alas, if I had found her alone, ‘I would have easily fixed arrow into her bow.’ ‘Neither I got hold of the enemy, nor could I pierce an arrow, ‘Neither I killed the enemy nor I captivated him.’ On the sixth day when he came he saw her sleeping with the queen in the similar manner. He was extremely up set and said to himself, ‘If I don’t see my enemy, I won’t make him to shed his blood. ‘Alas, I cannot keep my arrow contained in my bow. ‘And alas, I could not embrace the foe, ‘And neither could we copulate each other.’ Blind in love he did not try to acquiesce the reality. Neither, in excitement, he cared to learn the truth. Look, unaware what this king was doing, And was scheming to revel in such vices. Look, an ignorant scratches his head, And without wetting it, he shaves it. ‘Oh the Saki, give me my green cup, ‘So that without any infringement, I get the understanding. ‘And give me the cup full of green, ‘Which helps to destroy the enemies.
17.9: The Lord is One and the Victory is of the True Guru. You are the benevolent, pardoner of sins, and destroyer, Whatever is there in the universe, is all your creation. Neither you favour sons, nor brothers, Neither son-in-laws, nor enemies, nor friends, Listen to the tale of the King of Mayindra, Who was knowledgeable and was renown all over the world. He had a very intelligent person as his minister. Who was very shrewd and impressive. He was blessed with a son, whose thinking was logical too, Not only handsome, possessed brilliant qualities. He was known as a person with courageous heart, Through his manliness, he had blown up the enemies. one of the King's ministers was very shrewd, Who inspired the subject but perpetrated the enemies. That minister had a daughter, who was as illuminated as light, And her name was named 'Roshan Dimaagh'. The King admitted two of his children, Who had been sauntering too long, in school. They were admitted with a wise Maulana of Rome, Who had been endowed with wealth and land. Other children were present there too, Who used to read their lessons from the books. They all would bring their books tucked under their arms, Often there were discussions on Tohra and Anjeel. For the teaching of seven languages, two schools were established. One for the males; the other for the females. The boys were taught by a Maulana,, A knowledgeable lady instructed the girls. A wall was built between the two sections, The boys were kept on the one side and girls on the other. Both sides were endeavouring hard, To learn and excel over the other side, Everyone read all the books, Which were written both in Persian and Arabic. They discussed education among themselves, Irrespective of the fact whether they were intelligent or irrational. They raised the flags to acquire education for the swordsmanship, As soon as they reached the ages of maturity. As the spring season approached, In both the factions, the China syndrome sprung up. Like the King of kings of China, their desires rose, Particularly, the ladies achieved the beauteous treats. All of them blossomed like garden, And all the friends indulged in merriment. Inside that wall, a mouse used to live, Which had caused holes to appear in the wall. Through them two used to observe each other, One was the light of the universe and the other sun of the Yamanee Skies. Thus those two were trapped in the love affair, And they neglected their education and the worldly awareness. Their entanglement in the love was so intense, That both of them lost the senses of managing the stirrups of their horses. They both asked each other, ‘Oh the cherished one, you are like the sun, ‘And you, the Enlightener of the universe, and taking after the moon, how are you?’ When both of them were passing through such a state, Both, the male and female teachers, asked, ‘O, you the lamp of the skies and the Enlightener of the universe, ‘Why do you seem to be languishing? ‘Tell us, our loved ones, what has distressed you? Facially you look so weak? ‘Tell us about your afflictions so that we can suggest you remedies. ‘We may be able to prescribe some medicine.’ Both listened but did not try to respond, And hung their heads under the stress of love. When two, three or four days had lapsed, Both the bodies became conspicuous in love. The innocent childhood emotions were decimated, And the new sun came out with fresh inception. She was the daughter of a very genius, And she was extremely pretty and intelligent. He had recognised her from her apparent condition, He took her in seclusion and cordially said, ‘O you, the one as tall as cypress tree, moon-faced and silvery body, ‘You the light of the skies and sun of Yaman, ‘I cannot live without you, even for a moment. ‘May be we seem to be two bodies but we are one. ‘You tell me, how are you savouring? ‘My mind and body are always yearning for you. ‘To hide the fact from friends is erroneous. ‘To reveal the truth will be congenial for you and me. ‘If you reveal the truth to me, I will never betray, ‘And I swear this on my life. ‘To hide the fact from the friends is a sin, ‘Like the minister keeping secret from the king. ‘It is always beneficial to reveal and tell the fact. ‘Speaking the truth is the norm of a truthful mind.’ He asked repeatedly but there was no reply, Although she had expressed to seek truth. Then he arranged a social gathering with so much music, and a drinking spree, In which every one present in the assembly got drunk. They all were getting so much intoxicated, That what ever there was in their hearts, they were blabbing out. Their tongues were constantly reiterating, And except their lovers’ names, they were uttering nothing. Then the daughter of Maulana, arranged another social, Which was just for the colourful young and handsome. All of them became tipsy and inebriated, And passed over the limits if intellectuals. Any one who wanted to talk to them about education, They, being drunk, kept on repeating their lovers’ names. As the intellect and the presence of mind flew away, They kept on reciting each other’s names only. Every one who had some old friend, Would keep on repeating friends name again and again. As with such an action one was acknowledged as the lover, Who could speak cordially and looked handsome and happy. Those, who were imbued in love and smelled liquor, Could not remain hidden and, in due course, were revealed. The news spread in the city like a wild fire, That the son of the king and the daughter of the minister are openly in love. When the King heard this news, he asked for two boats. He put them both in separate ferries. He let loose both of them in the deep river, But through the waves both the vessels joined together. By the grace of God, both were reunited, And both, like the sun and the moon, were amalgamated. Look at the creation of Allah, the God Almighty, Through His order He merges the two bodies into one. United into one from two boats were two bodies, Of which one was light of Arabia and the other the moon of Yaman. The boats had floated and entered into the deep waters. And in the water they came floating like the spring leaves. There, sat a huge snake, Which pounced forward to eat them. From the other end appeared a ghost, Who raised her hands, which looked like headless pillars. The boat slipped through under the protection of the hands, And they both escaped the hidden intention of the snake, Which had intended to catch them to suck. But the All Benevolent saved their blood. A war between snake and ghost was imminent, But, by God’s grace, it did not occur. High waves sprung from the great river, And this secret, except God, no body could acquiesce. The rowing boat was struck with the high waves, And the incumbents prayed for escape. At the end with the will of God, the Almighty, The boat reached the safety of the bank. Both of them came out of the boat, And sat down on the banks of the river. Suddenly an alligator jumped out, To eat them both as if it was God’s will. Suddenly a lion appeared and it jumped ahead, It lunged over the water of the stream. They turned their heads, lion’s attack was deflected, And its futile bravery put in other’s mouth. The alligator caught half of lion with its paw, And dragged him into the deep water. Look at the creations of the Creator of the Universe, endowed them life and annihilated the lion. Both embarked to act according the will of God, One was King’s son and the other Minister’s daughter. They both occupied a derelict place to relax, So that they could not be noticed by any body, They both had reached a congenial and amicable country, And one was the son of the king and other the daughter of the minister. Then they reached the place where a king was seated, The king was as dark as night, and that black-ruler had a golden cap on. He saw them and called them nearer him, And said, ‘Oh my lion hearted ones and the ones of independent will, ‘What country you belong to and what is your name? ‘And who are you trying to find in this part of the world?’ ‘If you don’t tell me the truth, ‘Then, God witness, your death is certain.’ ‘I am the son of the ruler of the country of Mayindra, ‘And she is the daughter of the Minister.’ He narrated all what had happened previously, And explained all the afflictions they had passed through. He was overwhelmed with their affection, And said, ‘Consider my house as your own.’ ‘I hand over to you my ministerial affairs, ‘Along with that I will put several countries under your jurisdiction.’ With this pronouncement he was appointed the Minister, And given the title of Roshan Zameer, the enlightened consciousness. Whenever he encountered an enemy, With God’s benevolence, he raided the adversary. He would not hesitate to spill his own blood, And would do the same at any other rebellious place. Whenever he would shoot an arrow from his quiver, He would annihilate the enemy there and then. When a period of one year and four months had lapsed, He became as famous in the country as the moon in the sky, After stringing them through arrows he had nettled the enemies, And reminisced on the old days. One day the daughter of the minister said to him, ‘Oh, you the king of kings and the enlightened one, ‘Instantly you have forgotten your own country, ‘And being adorned with success, you have forgotten your own- self. ‘Remember your own country, ‘Where lies your paternal city. You must go and rehabilitate it.’ He had always been keeping vigil on this army, And had been distributing the wealth. One of the contingent, he decorated like the spring season. He provided thousands of daggers, and laced them with armours, Along with coat-of-mails, he gave them Hindustani swords, which were very heavy and expensive. Also the Guns from the country of Mashad, Including chain-mails of Rome and scimitars of Hindustan. They were provided with Arabian horses, outfitted with steel hooves. Along with all the stimulated elephants, which were as black as the night. All the fighters were very brave, They, the lion hearted ones, could decimate lines after lines. Although he was capable of killing an elephant, In the court he prevailed with very sweet tongue and wit. His spear was captivating, And the swords were tempered with the poison. A pyramid of the army was established, which was, Constituted of very handsome young-men, The daughter of the Minister put the turban on, And took a quiver full of arrows. Leading the frontal detachments, She led the army like the flowing river. Like a black cloud, when one contingent was despatched, The earth shook and the moon trembled. When the border was butted by the army, Which was equipped with arrows, swords and many other arms, And also provided were the weapons, Known as daggers, maces and slingshots, Then was plundered the country of Akleem, And one ruler took away the flying-horses and other outfits. The worn-torn country was left like, The trees, which are made barren during the fall. The defeat of the enemy opened all the annuls to march forward, And the opponents were left behind humiliated. Her fairy-like features depicted the lion’s courage, And she drew her dagger out of scabbard with great gusto. Who so ever she raided, she annihilated, And captured the place and claimed it as her own. When the ruler of Mayindra heard, He marched towards that place. He aligned his forces like the crops of spring, In opposition to the ones who were standing there fully armed. Like a wave from deep sea marched them, Who were shielded by the steel armour from head to feet. The uproars from guns, pistols and cannons overpowered, And earth became reddish like crimson flowers. She, herself, came into the fighting fields, With a Chinese bow in one hand and the arrows in the other. Whenever she hurtled them through her hands, The arrows pierced through the ribs of men and the elephants. The way the waves of the river struck the stones, The swords of the warriors were striking sparklingly. The brilliance of the shining was prevailing all over, And in the shine, the blood and the soil were indistinguishable. The swords of Hindustan glittered, And roared like thronging clouds over the river in flood. Chinese bows radiated, And the Hindustani swords glittered. The noises, which were overwhelming for many miles, Made the rivers desperate and severed the mountains. But when the swords of Yaman kindled, Both the sky and the earth kindled too. When a bamboo spear appeared coming fast, And the delicate lady flew in rage. The people raised a hue and cry, And the earth shook with the roar of guns. The bows and the slingshots came into action fiercely, And the Hindustani swords, shining like the mercury, commenced to penetrate. The blood sucking daggers appeared, And the lances, as sharp as snakes’ tongues, came into action. The shinning arms were gleaming, And earth was getting darker like the sulphur. Guns and the bows roared, and roared again, And the soldiers as huge as the crocodiles started to cry. The spontaneous sprinkle of showers from bows, Seemed as if the dooms day had come. Neither the foot soldiers had a place on earth, Nor the birds could find their ways through the air. The swords showed their feats in such intensity, That the dead bodies formed the mountains. The heaps of heads and feet were all over, And the whole field looked like golf course with heads rolling as balls. The intensity of the arrows was so great; That the armours and the hardtops were shattered. The swords were becoming as hot as the sun, And the trees were getting thirsty and river-water was drying. The showers of the arrows were so great, That only the necks of the elephants were visible. Instantly a Minister entered the field, And he drew the sword of Mayindra. From the other side the daughter came. She was holding a naked sword of Hindustan. The lightening swords became even swifter, And they tore off the enemy-hearts into pieces. She hit the enemy head with such vitality, That he was raised to ground like a crumbling mountain. The second one was cut with sword into two, And he fell flat like a wrecked mansion. Another intrepid person flew in like a hawk, But he was, too, exterminated. As soon this task was finished, And the relief was felt, third discordant surfaced, Another devil-like, drenched in blood, appeared, As if it had come straight from the hell. But he was cut into two as well and slaughtered, Like a lion slays an old antelope. The fourth valiant person entered the fight, Like a lion pounces upon a stag. It was hit with such a force, That it fell flat like a rider from the horse. When the fifth devil came, She begged for the God’s blessings, And hit him with such great intensity, That his head was trodden under the hooves of the horse. Revelling like a stupefied demon, the sixth devil came, As fast as an arrow shot out of the bow, But it was hit so rapidly that he was cut into two, And that caused the others to dread. This way about seventy such braves were annihilated, And hung over the tips of the swords, None other could dare to think of fight, Even the prominent warriors did not dare to come out. When the king, Mayindra, himself came into the fight, All the fighters rolled into wrath. And when the combatants jumped around, Both the earth and the heavens swayed. The lightening captured the universe, Like lustre of the swords of Yaman. The bows and slingshots were brought in action, And the ones beaten with maces raised hue and cries. Arrows and the gunshots prevailed, And the earth turned into red-flowery colour all around. When the blood-sucking daggers struck out, The shrieks flowed from the war-zones. When two of the steadfast warriors on the horsebacks entered the fighting, There was lighting all around. The way a Sraphil Angel appears and it becomes boisterous all over, the enemy was confused and disrupted. When it was raucous all around, The soldiers’ arms flickered in anger. The shinning ground turned and looked as if painted in red, The floor of a school with children reading sitting on top. Such a great number were killed, That they could not be enumerated. The king of Mayindra ran away, As most of his army was decimated. The Minister’s daughter pursued him, Caught him, tied him and made him prisoner. She brought the King to the ruler, And said, ‘Oh, you the king of kings, ‘He is the King of Mayindra, ‘Whom I have brought to you tied up. ‘If you order, I would kill him, ‘Or I would imprison him under lock and key.’ He was despatched to the big prison, And his canopy of the authority of ruling was snatched away. With the benevolence of the Provider, she attained the monarchy, After tearing off so many other sovereigns. Whosoever performs the deeds with such zeal, He is bestowed with His beneficence. The princess became the consort of the ruler, As she attained the kingdom with godly compassion., ‘Oh, Saki, give me the cup full of green liquid, ‘So that I may keep the secret enshroud. ‘Oh Saki! Give me the greenish wine of Europe, ‘Which I may need on the day of war.
17.10: The Lord is One and the Victory is of the True Guru. You are the guide of us who are trodden, And you are the rejuvenator of the hapless ones. You grant kingdom even to non-aspirants, The Heaven and the Earth, all function under Your command. Here now is the tale of the king of Kalandhar, Who had built a monumental gateway. He had a son who excelled in handsomeness, And whose intellect made him worthy of managing his countries’ affairs. At the same place, there was a daughter of a tycoon, She was as delicate as the leaves of a jasmine. That daughter fell in love with the son of the king, As much as the moon falls for the sun. She asked, ‘Oh, the prince, make me your spouse, ‘And do not care about any body else.’ ‘I have heard about the king of Hindustan, ‘The name of that strong man is Sher Shah. ‘The standard of morality in that God fearing country is such, ‘That no one can plunder even an iota of other’s rights. ‘To attain the kingdom, he had driven out the enemy, ‘ had dashed away like a cock in front of a falcon. ‘From the enemy, he had snatched two horses, ‘Which were brought from the country of Iraq. ‘Also, the enemy had presented him a lot of gold, and elephants, ‘Which were brought from across the Nile. ‘The name of one horse is Rahu and the other is Surahu. ‘Both are grand and their hooves are like the feet of the stags. ‘If you can fetch me both those horses, ‘Then, after that, I will marry you.’ Harking to this, she set out on her journey, And came to a city in the country of Sher Shah. She took her position on the bank of Jamuna. She brought with her wine and kebab to eat. When it was pitch dark and the night was through two watches, She floated a number of bundles of fodder. When the guards observed those bundles, They flew into rage. They fired guns on them a few times, But they were getting engulfed with the drowsiness. She repeated the process for three or four times, And at the end they were overpowered by the sleep. When she realised that the guards were slumbering, And they seemed like the injured soldiers, She walked and reached the place, Where there originated the base of the mansion. As the time-keeper hit the gong, She put the pegs in the wall. Climbing up the pegs, she reached the top of the building. With the blessings of God, she noticed both the horses. She hit one guard and cut him into two, Then at the door she destroyed two more. She met another one and cut his head off. She struck third one and made him to drench in blood. The fourth one was slashed and fifth decimated, The sixth became the victim of the handle of the dagger. After killing the sixth one, she leaped forward, And wanted to slaughter the seventh one who was standing on the platform. She injured the seventh one badly, And then, with the blessing of God, stretched her hand towards the horse. She mounted the horse and hit him so hard, That it jumped over the wall and into the river Jamuna. For long time, the horse paddled around in water, In the mean time the King of the Land came to know of the happening. Sher Shah, the king, bit his hand, And he was extremely put in predicament of the action. ‘How has one taken my superb horse? ‘On God’s honour, I will pardon him, he pronounced, ‘If I see that person, ‘I will forgive him and endow him a treasure. ‘Strange enough, if I ever come across him, ‘I will never fly into rage. ‘If he comes voluntarily, ‘I will further give him one hundred bags full of coins.’ Through out the city, it was proclaimed, ‘I will forgive that robber but he must come to see me at least once.’ Then the daughter of the tycoon, wearing golden turban, And holding a shinning shield, presented herself, And said, ‘Oh, Sher Shah, the killer of lions, ‘It is me who had taken your horse in a strange way.’ Listening to her the intelligent king was astounded. And once again rapidly asked, ‘Oh you the fast one, tell me how did you do it? ‘To show me, you come and replay.’ She sat down on the bank of river, And the same way she drank wine and ate kebob. Then she floated the bundles of the grass, And this way deceived the king’s guards. To show her cleverness of going across the river, She swam over the rough water. She killed the first guard in a similar manner, And vanished like the dust. When the sun was just set, She came to the same place and untied the second horse. After bridling, she mounted the horse, And then she hit the satanic animal. The horse flew so high, That it glided over the head of the king and jumped into the river. Swimming over the great river, With God’s blessings, the horse went across. She dismounted, saluted the King, And communicated aloud in Arabic. ‘Oh, Sher Shah, why did you let your intelligent dispel. ‘I had taken Rahu myself but now you, yourself, gave me Surahus.’ Declaring thus she galloped the horse, And she thanked the Great Benevolent Almighty. She was pursued by numerous horse-riders, But none could reach to catch her. All his warriors threw their turbans in front of the King, ‘Oh, the King of the universe and the provider, ‘No one could dare to take away those horses, ‘But you gave her one yourself. ‘Why, sire, did you take an oblivious decision. ‘Rahu, she had stolen but you gave her Surahu yourself.’ Both the horses she took away, And, with godly compassion, she handed over them to her friend. He married her and brought her home, And, with celestial grace, full-filled his promise., ‘Give me the cup full of liquidated poppy-husk, ‘Which may help me at the time of struggle. ‘Also it is reliable to beat the enemy. ‘Even one sip of this makes one feel like an elephant.’
17.11: The Lord is One and the Victory is of the True Guru. He is blissful and endows abundance of amenities He is nurturer and emancipators He is compassionate and provider of shelter He is magnanimous and knows all in the earth and heavens I have heard a Tale at the lofty Khaiber Mountains There lived a Pathan whose name was Raheem He had a wife who was as delightful as moon Her looks alone were homicidal for many a Princes Like the clouds of rainy-season her eyelashes had electrifying effect Which struck them like arrows The shine from her face made them to forget even the moon To all the Princes she was epitome of the garden in the spring Her eyelids were twined like a bow And they shot out calamitous arrows Her looks accorded the ecstasy of wine And as well as desolated the blooming gardens She was ravishingly beautiful and surpassed all norms of exquisiteness She was graceful no doubt but she possessed archaic thought There lived a Pathan called Hassan Khan at the same place The wisdom of his thought was quite mature They both loved each other so much That even Majnu and Laila would have been envious of them The love in them became so intense That they lost the control of reins and stirrups She invited him home all alone And seeing him she was over-powered with lust When eating and drinking two three and four months had passed by One of their enemies informed the Master Raheem Khan Pathan flew into rage And roaring drew his sword from the scabbard When she received the news that her husband was coming She killed that man with a sword She put his meat in a saucepan added spices And put it on fire She served that cooked meat to her husband With what was left over she entertained the servants Her husband was satisfied that there was no other person there He went back and killed the person who had brought the news ‘Oh! Saki Give me the cup full of green ‘Which I need at the time of struggle ‘Fill it up to the brim so that I can drink it with every breath ‘And forget the afflictions of both the worlds

3 Part 1.1: The Lord is One and He can be attained through the grace of the true Guru. Now the Granth entitled ‘BACHITTAR NATAK’ is composed. From the Holy Mouth of the Tenth King DOHRA I salute the Glorious SWORD with all my heart’s affection. I shall complete this Granth only if Thou Helpest me. I.
3 Part 1.2: The Eulogy of the Revered Death. The sword chops well, chops the forces of fools and this mighty one bedecks and glorifies the battlefield. It is the unbreakable staff of the arm, it has the powerful luster and its light even bedims the radiance of the sum. It brings happiness to the saints, mashing the vicious ones, it is the destroyer of sins and I and under its refuge. Hail, hail to the cause of the world, saviour of the universe, it is my preserver, I hail its victory.
3 Part 1.3: He, who is ever light-incarnate and birthless entity, Who is the god of chief gods, the king of chief kings Who is Formless, Eternal, Amorphous and Ultimate Bliss Who is the Cause of all the Powers, I salute the wielder of the Sword. 3 He is Formless, Flawless, eternal and Non-aligned He is neither distinctively old, nor young nor immature; He is neither poor nor rich; He is Formless and Markless He is Colourless, Non-attached, Limitless and Guiseless. 4; He is Formless, Signless, Colourless and Non-attached; He is Nameless, Placeless; and a Radiating Great Effulgence He is Blemishless, Guiseless, Formless and Eternal He is a Superb Practising Yogi and a Supremely Holy Entity. 5 He is unconquerable, Indistinguishable, Nameless and Placeless He is a Superb Practicing Yogi, He is the Supreme Ravisher He is Accountless, Garbless, Stainless and without Beginning He is in the Yond, Immaculate and ever without Contention. 6 He is the Primal, Orignless, Stainless and Endless He is Blemishless, Guiseless, Master of the earth and the destroyer of Pride He is Ireless, Ever fresh, Deceitless and Non-attached He is Lustless, Angerless, Birthless and Sightless. 7 He is in the Yond, Immaculate, Most Holy and Ancient He is Unconquerable, Indistinguishable, Will be in future and is always Present He is without ailment and sorrow and is ever new He is Birthless, He is the Supporter and is Supremely dexterous. 8 He Pervades in the Past, Future and Present I Salute Him, Who is without vices and without ailments I Salute Him, Who is the god of gods and king of kings He is Supportless, Eternal and Greatest of Emperors. 9 He is Accountless, Guiseless, Elementless and Blemishless He is without attachment, colour, form and mark He is the Greatest of gods and the Supreme Yogi He is the Greatest of the rapturous and the greatest of the Ravishing. 10 Somewhere He bears the quality of rajas, somewhere tamas and somewhere sattva Somewhere He takes the form of a woman and somewhere man Somewhere He manifests Himself as a goddess, god and demon Somewhere He appears in several unique forms. 11 Somewhere He, taking the form of a flower, is rightly puffed up Somewhere becoming a black bee, seems inebriated Somewhere becoming the wind, moves with such speed, Which is indescribable, how can I elucidate it?. 12 Somewhere He become a musical instrument, which is played appropriately Somewhere He becomes a hunter who looks glorious with His arrow Somewhere He becomes a deer and allures exquisitely Somewhere He manifests Himself as Cupid’s wife, with impressive beauty. 13 His Form and Mark cannot be comprehended Where doth He live and what guise doth He adopt? What is His Name and how he is called? How can I describle? He is Indescribable. 14 He hath no father, mother and brother He hath no son, no grandson and no male and female nurses He hath no attachment, no home, no army and no companion He is the Great King of kings and Great Lord of lords. 15 He is Supreme, Ancient, Immaculate and in the Yond He is beginningless Stainless, Non-existent and Unconquerable He is Indistinguishable, Indestructible, Holy and Paramount He is the Most Humble of the meek and Great Lord of lords. 16 He is Stainless, Imperishable, Accountless and Guiseless He is Limitless, Blemishless, Formless and Maliceless He is the Most Effulgent of all lights and Supreme Conflagration of all fires He is the Supreme Spell of all incantations and Supreme embodiment of Death over all such powers. 17 He holds the bow in His left hand and the terrible sword He is the Supreme Effulgence of all lights and sits in His Great Glory He, of Infinite Splendour, is the masher of of the boar-incarnation with great grinder tooth He crushed and devoured thousands of the creatures of the world. 18 The tabor resounds and the black and white canopy swings Loud laughter emanates from his mouth and the weapons glisten His conch produces such a terrible sound That appears like the blazing fire of the Death on doomsday.
3 Part 1.4: Many gongs resound and hearing their sound,! The clouds feel ashamed! Such a sound is produced that it appears! Like the sound of the surging waves of the sea! 20 The small bells of the feet jingle,! And the anklets rattle! Such sounds are peaceful sounds ! Against the great resounding! 21 The rosary of heads glorified his neck, ! Seeing which the god Shiva feels abashed! Such a beautiful image appears magnificent ! And it is greatly holy! 22 He produces the very loud roar, ! Hearing which the messengers tremble! The blood oozes glorifying his neck ! And it is fascinating his great honour!
3 Part 1.5: STANZA! Thou hast created the Svetaja, Jeraju and Uddahhujja division of creation. ! Like this Thou hast created the Andaja division and also the regions and universes! Thou hast also created the directions, the indivcations, the earth and the sky. ! Thou hast also related the four Vedas, the Quran and the Puranas! 24 Thou hast created night and day and established the sun and moon. ! Thou hast created gods and demons of the mighty Death hath subdued all! Thou hast created the pen to write on the tablet and hast recorded the writ on the forehead. ! The hand of the mighty Death hath subdued all! 25 He hath effaced many and then made others.! He destroys the created ones and then creates after effacing! None could comprehend the working of Death.! Many have experienced it and many will experience it! 26 Somewhere He hath created millions of the servants like Krishna.! Somewhere He hath effaced and then created like Rama! Many Muhammads had been on the earth. ! They were born and then died in their own times! 27 All the Prophets and saints of the past were conquered by Death,! But none could conquer it! All the incarnations of Vishnu like Rama and Krishan were destroyed by KAL,! But they could not destroy him! 28 All the indras and Chandras who came into being were destroyed by KAL,! But they could not destroy him! All those Prophets, saints and hermits, who came into being,! Were all ultimately crushed under the grinder tooth of KAL! 29 All the glorious kings like Mandhata were all bound down ! And thrown in the noose of KAL! Those who have remembered the Name of the Lord, have been saved, ! Without coming under His refuge, millions are considered as having been killed by KAL!
3 Part 1.6: The sword of KAL glistens Which is Non-elemental and terrible. While moving his anklets rattle And the small bells jingle. He hath four winsome arms and on his head His long hair have been bound in a lovely knot. The mace with him appears splendid Which fascinate the honour of Yama. His tongue red like fire seems magnificent And his grinder teeth are very frightening. His conches and drums resound Like the thundering sound of the sea. His dark form looks elegant And is the abode of Great Glory. On his face there are lovely delineations Which are superbly holy.
3 Part 1.7: On his head there swings the beautiful lustrous and white canopy Seeing whose shadow and considering it winsome , the light feels abashed. The fleshy and red eyes of the God seem magnificent Before whose light millions of suns appear irritated. Somewhere He appears impressive in the semblance of a Great King Somewhere He allures the minds of apsaras or the daughters of gods. Somewhere as a warrior He holds the bow in his hand Somewhere as a king he causes the resounding of his trumpets.
3 Part 1.8: He seems bedecked beautifully Wielding his bow and arrows. He holds the sword Like a great warrior. He is forcefully engaged in war Fighting frightening battles. He is the treasure of mercy And ever kind. He is always the same And the monarch of all. He is Unconquerable and birthless And helps those who come under His refuge. The sword shines in His hand And He is a Great Donor for the people. I salute the Supreme KAL Who is unique in the present and shall be unique in future. He is the effacer of the pride of the demon Madhu And the destroyer of the demon Sumbh. He hath white canopy over His head And the weapons glisten in His hands. Hearing His loud voice The great monarchs are frightened. He wears elegantly the garments of directions And listening to His voice the sorrows run away. Hearing His call The infinite happiness is attained. He is Shyam in the form of clouds And appears beautiful and impressive. He hath four beautiful arms And is wearing crown on the head. The mace conch and disc glisten And seem frightful and resplendent.
3 Part 1.9: The unique beauty appears graceful And on seeing it the Cupid seems ashamed. In the worlds it has supernatural radiance Seeting whichall the people are fascinated. The moon is bearning on his head Seeing which the god Shiva feels shy. The ornaments of Nagas bedeck his neck. Which have the power of destruction for the tyrants. He who wields the sword in his hand He is the remover of millions of sins. He hath caught hold of the big mace And hath fitted the arrow in his stretched bow. There is sound of the blowing conch And jingling of many small bells. O Lord I have come under Thy Refuge Protect my honour. Thou appearest impressive in various forms And gods and are the treasure of the Grace alone. Thou art the worshipping temple of the demons And gods and are the treasure of the Grace alone . He remain uniform from the beginning to end And hath adopted various forms. The sword appears impressive in his hand Seeing which the sins run away. His body is bedecked with ornaments Which allures both body and mind. The arrow is fitted in the bow Which causes many enemies to flee away. There is the jingling sound of the small bells And a new sound emanates from the anklets. There is light like the blazing fire and lightning Which is highly holy and pure.
3 Part 1.10: Various kinds of pure tunes emanate from the anklets. The face appears like the in blaze of lightning the dark clouds. His gait is like that of an elephant Intoxicated with wine. His loud thunder appears like the roar of a cub in the forest.53 Thou art in the world in the past Future and present. Thou art the ONLY ONE Saviour in the Iron age. Thou art ever new continuously at all places. Thou appearest impressive and sweet in Thy Blissful form. Thou hast two grinder teeth. Terrible white and high Seeing which the tyrants run away from the battlefield. Thou art inebriated holding the terrible sword in Thy hand . Both the gods and demons sing the eulogy of His victory. When the united sound of the girdle bells and the anklets emantes Then all the mountains become restless like mercury and the earth trembles. When the constant jingling loud sound is heard Then all the movable and immovable objects become restless. Thy weapons are used in all the fourteen worlds alongwith Thy Command the empty ones. With which Thou causest deficiency in the augmented once and fill to the brim All the creatures of the world on land and in water Who is the amongst them who hath the audacity to refuse Thy Command? Just as the dark cloud seem impressive in the month of Bhadon In the same manner Thy dark body hath its glow. The chain of Thy teeth glitters like lightning The melody of the small bells and gongs is like the thunder of the clouds.
3 Part 1.11: Thy beauty appears elegant like the dark clouds of the month of Sawan Comprehending Thy beautiful form the mountain of blue gems hath bent its head. The most beautiful black colour highly fascinates the mind Thou art the most beautiful of the beautiful once and the most passionate of he passionate once. The Order of KAL is prevalent in all the fourteen worlds. Who is the other one who hath the audacity to refuse His Order? Tell me , in which direction you can flee and remain safe? Since the KAL dances over the heads of all. Through one may erect millions of forts and may remain under their protection Even then in the case of a blow of KAL he will not be saved in any way. Though one may write many Yantras and recite millions of mantras Even then he cannot be saved. No other shelter can save one without His refuge. The writers of Yantras have grown weary and the reciters of mantras have accepted defeat. But ultimately they all have been destroyed by KAL. Many Tantras have been tamed and in such endeavours one hath wasted his birth. All have become useless and none hath proved useful. Many have become Brahmacharis and have closed their nostrils. Many have worn Kanthi on their necks and have matted hair on their heads. Many have got their ears perforated and caused others to call them great Yogis. All such religious observances were useless and none of them became useful. There had been mighty demon-kings like Madhu and Kaitabh The KAL crushed them on their turn. Then there were Sumbah Nisumbh and Sranavat Beef. They were also chopped into bits by KAL. The mighty king Prithu and the great sovereign like Mandhata Who had demarcated seven continents with his chariot-wheel. The king Bhim and the Bharat, who had conquered and brought the world under their control with the strength of arms . They were all destroyed by KAL when they were nearing their end. He who hath created the frightening dominance of His Name. He who had snatched the earth from the Kshatriyas with the strength of staff-like arms. He who had performed millions of Yajnas and erned multi-faceted approbation. Even that winsome warrior hath been conquered by KAL. Those who had conquered millions of forts and razed them. Those who had treaded the forces of innumerable warriors. Those who had indulged in many wars events and disputes I have seen them subdued and killed by KAL.67 Those who had ruled for millions of ages And had enjoyed nicely the pleasures and vicious tastes. They had ultimately gone with naked feet. I have seen them having been subdued Fallen and killed by the persistent KAL. He who had destroyed many kings He who had enslaved the moon and the sun in his house. He had conquered the god Indra in war And later released him. I have seen being subdued fallen and killed by KAL.
3 Part 1.12: All the Ramas who incarnated, Ultimately passed away. All the Krishnas, who had incarnated, Have all passed away. All the gods who will come into being in future, They will all ultimately expire. All the Buddhas, who came into being, Expired ultimately. All the god-kings, who came into being, Ultimately passed away. All the demon-kings, who came into being, They were all destroyed by KAL. The incarnation Narsingh Was also killed by KAL. The incarnation with grinder teeth Was killed by mighty KAL. Vaman, the Brahmin incarnation, Was killed by KAL. The Fish incarnation of spatious mouth, Was entrapped by KAL. All those who had come into being, They were all conquered by KAL. Those who will go under His Refuge, They will all be saved by him.
3 Part 1.13: Without coming under His Refuge, there is no other measure for protection, May be a god, demon, pauper or a king. May be the Sovereign and may be the courtiers, Without coming under His shelter, millions of measures for protection will be useless. All the creatures created by Him in the world Will ultimately be killed by the mighty KAL. There is no other protection without coming under His shelter, Even though many Yantras be written and millions of Mantras be recited.
3 Part 1.14: All the kings and pupers who have come into being, Are sure to be killed by KAL. All the Lokpals, who have come into being, Will ultimately be mashed by KAL. Those who meditate on the Supreme KAL, The wielder of the sword, they firmly adopt innumerable measures for protection. Those who remember KAL, They conquer the world and depart. That Supreme KAL is Supremely Pure, Whose image is supernatural and winsome. He is bedecked with supernatural beauty, All the sins flee on hearing His Name. He, who hath wide and red eyes, And who is the destroyer of innumerable sins. The glitter of his face is more beautiful than that of the moon And who hath caused many sinners to ferry across.
3 Part 1.15: All the Lokpals Are subservient to KAL. All the suns and moons and Even Indra and Vaman (are subservient to KAL.
3 Part 1.16: All the fourteen worlds are under the Command of KAL. He hath stringed all the Naths by turning about the slanting evebrows. May be Rama and Krishna, may be the moon and sun, All are standing with folded hands in the presence of KAL.
3 Part 1.17: At the instance of KAL, Vishnu appeared, whose power is manifested through the world. At the instance of KAL, Brahma appeared and also at the instance of KAL the Yogi Shiva appeared. At the instance of KAL, the gods, demons, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Bhujang, directions and indications have appeared. All the other prevalent object are within KAL, only One supreme KAL is ever Timeless and eternal.
3 Part 1.18: Salutation to the God of gods and salutation to the wielder of sword, Who is ever monomorphic and ever without vices. Salutation to Him, who manifests the qualities of activity, rhythm and morbidity. Salutation to Him who is without vices and who is without ailments.
3 Part 1.19: Salutation to Him, who wields the bow in his hands Salutation to Him, who is Fearless. Salutation to Him, who is God of gods. Salutation to Him, Who shall ever be within the world.
3 Part 1.20: Salutation to him, who wields spear, double-edged sword, sword and dagger, Who is ever monomorphic and ever without vices. Salutation to Him, who is the wielder of bow in His hands and who also carries the staff, Who hath spread His Light in all the fourteen worlds. I salute the arrow and the gun, I salute the lustrous sword, Which Is impenetratable and indestructible. I salute the great mace and lance, Which have no equal or second in bravery.
3 Part 1.21: Salutation to Him, Who holds the disc in His hand, He hath manifested Himself without elements. Salutation to Him, who hath sharp grinder teeth, Which are thick and strong. Salutation to Him, who hath the arrows and the cannon, Who hath destroyed the enemies. Salutation to Him, Who holds the straight sword and the bayonet, Who hath reporimanded the tyrants. I salute all the weapons of various names. I salute all the weapons of various names. I salute all kinds of armour I salute all kinds of armour.
3 Part 1.22: There is no other support for the poor except Thee, who hath made me a mountain from a straw. O Lord! Forgive me for my mistakes, because who is there so much blunderhead like me? Those who have served Thee, there seems wealth and self-confidence in all there homes. In this Iron age, the supreme trust is only for KAL, Who is the Sword-incarnate and hath mighty arms. He, who hath destroyed millions of demons like Sumbh and Nisumbh in and instant. Who hath annihilated in and instant the demons like Dhumarlochan, Chand, Mund and Mahishasura. Who hath immediately thrashed and thrown down far away the demons like Chamar, Ranchichchhar and Rakat Beej. On realizing the Lord like Thee, this servant of yours doth not care for anyone else. He, Who hath mashed millions of demons like Mundakasura, Madhu, Kaitabh, Murs and Aghasura. And such heroes who never asked anyone for support in the battlefield and had never turned back even two feet. And such demons, who could not be drowned even in the sea and there was no impact on them of the fireshafts. On seeing Thy Sword and forsaking their shyness, they are fleeing away. Thou hast destroyed in and instant the warriors like Ravana, Kumbhkarna and Ghatksura. And like Meghnad, who could defeat even Yama in the war.. And the demons like Kumbh and Akumbh, who conquering all, washed away the blood from their weapons in seven seas, etc. All of them died with the terrible sword of the mighty KAL. If one tries to flee and escape from KAL, then tell in which direction shall he flee? Wherever one may go, even there he will perceive the well-seated thundering sword of KAL. None hath been able to tell uptil now the measure, which, may be adopted to save himself from the blow of KAL. O foolish mind! The one from whom Thou cannot escape in any manner, why doth thee not go under His Refuge. Thou hast meditated on millions of Krishnas, Vishnus, Ramas and Rahims. Thou hast recited the name of Brahma and established Shivalingam, even then none could save thee. Thou hast observed millions of austerities for millions of days, but thou couldst not be recompensed even for the value of a couldst not be recompensed even for the value of a cowrie. The Mantra recited for fulfillment of worldly desires doth not even bring the least gain and none of such Mantras can’t save from the blow of KAL. Why doth thou indulge in false austerities, because they will not bring in gain of even one cowrie. The cannot save themselves form the blow, how can they protect thee? They are all hanging in the blazing fire of anger, therefore they will cause thy hanging similarly. O fool! Ruminate now in thy mind; none will be of any use to thee except the grace of KAL. O foolish beast! Thou doth not recognize Him, Whose Glory hath spread over all the three worlds. Thou worshippest those as God, by whose touch thou shalt be driven far away from the next world. Thou art committing such sins in th name of parmarath that by committing them the Great sins may feel shy. O fool! Fall at the feet of Lord-God, the Lord is not within the stone-idols. The Lord cannot be realized by observing silence, by forsaking pride, by adopting guises and by shaving the head. He cannot be realized by wearing Kanthi for severe austerities or Thy making a knot of matted hair on the head. Listen attentively, I speak Turth, Thou shalt not achieve the target without going under the Refuge of the LORD, Who is ever Merciful to the lowly. God can only be realized with LOVE, He is not pleased by circumcision. If all the continents are transformed into paper and all the seven seas into ink By chopping all the vegetation the pen may be made for the sake of writing If the goddess Saraswati be made the speaker and Ganesha be there to write with hands for millions of ages Even then, O God! O sword-incannate KAL! Without supplication, none can make Thee pleased even a little. Here ends the First Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled The Eulogy of Sri KAL.’
3 Part 1.23: AUTOBIOGRAPHY CHAUPAI O Lord! Thy Praise is Supreme and Infinite, None could comprehend its limits. O God of gods and King of kings, The Merciful Lord of the lowly and protector of the humble.
3 Part 1.24: The dumb utters the six Shastras and the crippled climbs the mountain. The blind one sees and the deaf listens, if the KAL becomes Gracious.
3 Part 1.25: O God! My intellect is trifling. How can it narrate Thy Praise? I cannot praise Thee, Thou mayst Thyself improve this narration. Upto what limit this insect can depict? Thou mayst Thyself improve Thy Greatness. Just as the son cannot say anything about the birth of his father Then how can one unfold Thy mystery. Thy Greatness is Only Thine It cannot be described by others. O Lord! Only Thou knowest Thy doings. Who hast the power to elucidate Thy High of Low acts? Thou hast made one thousand hoods of Sheshanaga Which contain two thousand tongues. He is reciting till now Thy Infinite Names Even then he hath not know the end of Thy Names. What can one say about Thy doings? One gets puzzled while understanding it. Thy subtle form is indescribable I speak about Thy Immanent Form. When I shall observe Thy loving Devotion I shall then describe all Thy anecdotes from the beginning. Now I narrate my own life-story How the Sodhi clan came into being.
3 Part 1.26: With the concentration of my mind, I narrate in brief my earlier story. Then after that, I shall relate all in great detail.
3 Part 1.27: In the beginning when KAL created the world It was brought into being by Aumkara. Kal sain was the first king Who was of immeasurable strength and supreme beauty. Kalket became the second king And Kurabaras, the third. Kaldhuj was the fourth kin From whon the whole world originated. He had a thousand eyes and thousand feet. He slept on Sheshanaga Therefore he was called the master of Shesha. Out of the secretion from one of his ears Madhu and Kaitabh came into being. And from the secretion of the other ear The whole world materialized. After some period the Lord killed the demons. Their marrow flowed into the ocean. The greasy substance floated thereon because of that medital The earth was called medha. Because of virtuous actions A purusha is known as devta And because of evil actions He is known as asura. If everything is described in detail It is feared that the description will become voluminous. There were many kings after Kaldhuj Like Daksha Prajapati etc. Ten thousand daughters were born to them Whose beauty was not matched by others. In due course all these daughters Were married with the kings.
3 Part 1.28: Banita, Kadaru, Diti and Aditi became the wives of sages, And Nagas, their enemies, the gods and demons were born to them.
3 Part 1.29: From that, the sun was born, from whom Suraj Vansh originated. If I describe the names of the kings of this of this clan, I fear a great extension of the story. In this clan, there was a king named Raghu, who was the originator of Raghuvansh in the world. He had a great son Aja, a mighty warrior and superb archer. When he renounced the world as a Yogi, he passed on his kingdom to his son Dastratha. Who had been a great archer and had married three wives with pleasure. The eldest one gave birth to Rama, the others gave birth to Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughan. They ruled over their kingdom for a long time, after which they left for their heavenly abode. After that the two sons of Sita became the kings. They married the Punjabi princesses and performed various types of sacrifices. There they founded two cities, the one Kasur and the other Lahore. Both the cities surpassed in beauty to that of Lanka and Amravati. For a long time, both the brothers ruled over their kingdom and ultimately they were bound down by the noose of death. After them their sons and grandson ruled over the world. They were innumerable, therefore it is difficult to describe all. It is not possible to count the names of all those who ruled over their kingdoms in all the four ages. If now you shower your grace upon me, I shall describe names, as I know them. Kalket and Kal Rai had innumerable descendants. Kalket was a mighty warrior, who drove out Kal Rai from his city. Kal Rai settled in the country named Sanaudh and married the king’s daughter. A son was born to him, who was named Sodhi Rai. Sodhi Rai was the founder of Sanaudh dynasty by the Will of the Supreme Purusha. His sons and grandsons were called sodhis. They became very famous in the world and gradually prospered in wealth. They ruled over the country in various ways and subdued kings of many countries. They extended their Dharma everywhere and had the royal canopy over their head. They performed Rajasu sacrifice several times declaring themselves as supreme rulers, after conquering kings of various countries. They performed Bajmedh-sacrifice several times, clearing their dynasty of all the blemishes. After that there arose quarrels and differences within the dynasty, and none could set the things right. The great warriors and archers moved towards the battlefield for a fight. The world hath perished after quarrel on wealth and property from very olden times. The attachment, ego and infights spread widely and the world was conquered by lust and anger.
3 Part 1.30: The mammon may hailed, who hath the whole world as her slave. All the world goes in search for her and all go to salute her.
3 Part 1.31: None could remember KAL and there was only extension of enmity, strife ego. Only greed become the base of the world, because of which everyone wants the other to die. End of the Second Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled ‘The Description of Ancestry’.
3 Part 1.32: The Providence created the great vices of enmity and strife, which could not be controlled by any reformer. Which warrior could save himself from the blwos of mighty king lust and the great courtiers creed and attachment? There the youthful warriors are busy challenging shuts amongst themselves, they stand up with their weapons and are engaged in tough fight. In this fight, somewhere there are innumerable shafts, helmets and double-edged swords in use. The evil spirits and ghosts are dancing and the tabors are resounding. Somewhere the god Shiva is stringing the skulls in his rosary of skulls, somewhere the vampires and ghosts are shrieking joyfully. Somewhere the terrible goddess Chamunda is shouting and somewhere the vultures are shrieking. Somewhere the corpses of youthful warriors are lying inter-lovked. There had been tough battle, because of which the chopped corpses are rolling in dush. Somewhere the dead warriors are lying uncared with their hands on their whiskers. Somewhere the skulls, helmets, bows and arrows are lying scattered. Somewhere the swords and quivers of the warriors are there in the battlefield. Somewhere the vultures shriek and somewhere the vampire is belching. Somewhere the evil spirits and ghosts are walking slantingly, somewhere the ghosts, fiends and meateaters are laughing.
3 Part 1.33: Hearing the thunder of minghty warriors, the clouds felt shy. Strong banners have been fixed and highly infuriated the heroes are enaged in war. Holding their swords and daggers, they are fighting in great anger. The winsome great heroes, with their fighting, make the earth tremble. The warriors are fighting with their weapons in great excitement, the weapons as well as the armour are glistening. There is the great steel-killing with weapons like swords and daggers.
3 Part 1.34: Various types of swords, the swords from Halab and Junab, Sarohi swords and the double-deged sword, knife, spear and dagger were struck with great ire. Somewhere the lancet and somewhere the pike only were used, somewhere the lance and the dagger were being used violently.
3 Part 1.35: The warriors are fiercely adorned with weapons, with which tthey fight forsaking all doubts. Without hesitation they strike the weapons and chop the limbs. They do not care at all and shout “kill, kill”. They challenge and drive with force and endure the blows of many weapons. Thousand of houris move in the sky; they move forward to marry the martyrs. The warriors move in the battlefield in a frightful manner, and utter “kill, kill” The limbs of some warrior have been chopped and the hair of some have been uprooted. The flesh of someone has been peeled and someone hath fallen after being chopped. There is knocking sound of drums and shield. The frontline army hath been uprooted. The warriors strike their weapons very quickly and trample over the heroic army. New trumpets resound and the mighty warriors with quality of forbearance, roar. They strike the swords and shoot the arrows and suddenly chop away the limbs. Filled with anger, they move forward and do not go back even four feet. They hold the weapons and challenge and hearing their thunder, the clouds feel shy. They raise their heart-rending shouts and strike their weapons violently. They fight, forgetting all sorrows and several of them move towards heaven. The warriors filled with ire and moving forward shoot a volley of arrows. The conch is blown and in such a terrible time, the warriors get adorned with patience.
3 Part 1.36: The trumpet and conch resound and the great warriors look impressive. The swift-running horses dance and the brave warriors are excited. The glistening sharp swords flash like lightning. The sound of drums arises and is heard continuously. Somewhere the double-edged swords and helmets lie broken, somewhere the warriors shout “kill, kill”. Somewhere the warriors are forcefully knocked about and somewhere, being puzzled, they have fallen down. The great army is being trampled and limbs are being chopped into halves. The long steel maces are struck and the shouts of “kill, kill” are raised. The stream of blood is full and the houris walk over the sky. The goddess Kali is thundering in the sky and the vamps are laughing. The great warriors equipped with steel and filled with ire look impressive. They roar with great pride and hearing them, the clouds feel shy. The warriors are adorned with steel-weapons and shout “kill, kill”. They have slanting whiskers on their faces and fight without caring for their life. There are shouts and the army hath laid the siege. In great anger the warriors rush from all sides shouting “kill, kill”. The warriors are meeting with their lances like the Ganges with the sea. Many of them under cover of their shields even break the striking swards with cracking sound. There are shouts after shouts and the swift-running horses dance. The warriors are highly ferocious and are fighting with the awakening of anger. The sharp lances have fallen down and there is great knocking. The eaters of flesh are dancing and the warriors are engaged in hot war. The flesh-eating creatures are laughing and the gangs of ghosts are dancing.
